members.note: UMG's blur is a single-child panel; this one is a VISUAL you put on a widget, so it holds nothing of its own. What is inside the blurred widget is arranged by that widget's own slot, which carries the padding.
Same reason as Padding: the arrangement is the slot's, because the blur is a look rather than a container.
Named without this codebase's bool prefix here because the property predates it and is already saved in assets.

How far the blur REACHES, parameterized differently. UMG takes a kernel radius in pixels and, unless bOverrideAutoRadiusCalculation is ticked, computes it from the strength anyway. This blur is a down-sample chain: the reach is the strength (0..1) spread over up to MaxDownSampleLevel halvings, so it is always UMG's non-overridden mode, and the override has nothing to override.

The blurred region's SHAPE is a mask here rather than a radius: the mask texture's red channel decides which pixels of the rect are blurred, so a rounded-corner mask gives exactly UMG's rounded blur, and any other silhouette besides. MaskTextureUVRect places it.

There is no quality gate to fall back FROM. UMG's brush is drawn when Slate's renderer reports that blur is unavailable or the scalability setting turned it off; nothing in this pipeline asks that question -- the proxy renders whenever BlurStrength is above zero and is skipped when it is not. A project that wants a cheap version sets BlurStrength to 0 and skins the widget the blur sits on, which is what the fallback brush is.
Marks the render proxy dirty, which a bare property write does not -- hence the BlueprintSetter on the property.
See BlurRadius above; both mark the render proxy dirty.
